findings: VERIFIED (r1 advisories resolved): workflow_policy() now compares full filenames from directory.iterdir() against an exact expected set, so a duplicate-stem twin (interpret.yaml beside interpret.yml) changes the inventory and is refused; this is directly covered by test_duplicate_yaml_and_ci_write_permissions_rejected. check.yml content is now inspected: [push, pull_request] triggers, top-level contents: read, single 'basic' job, no job- or step-level permissions overrides, persist-credentials: false on every checkout, and no 'secrets.' text. test_branch_names_are_not_review_pins now passes the resolved repo root instead of '.', removing the cwd fragility.

VERIFIED (quarantine, fail-closed): all six model workflows must exact-match the CONDITION string (workflow_dispatch + pilot ref + pilot destination input + PILOT_REMOTE_RESEARCH_ENABLED), end in a terminal guard whose run text must fullmatch a closed echo-'BLOCKED: ...'/exit-1 regex and which is executed and required to return exit code 1 with a BLOCKED prefix; exactly one other run step pinned byte-for-byte to the workflow_boundary verify command; only three SHA-pinned actions allowed; exactly one checkout bound to {ref: github.sha, fetch-depth: 1, persist-credentials: false}; results-validate.yml must keep contents: read, a single job, and if: '${{ false }}'. Structural lookups (data['permissions'], job['steps']) raise on absence, so malformed workflows fail closed.

VERIFIED (identity bindings): verify() refuses to run outside its own checkout (resolved root must equal the script's parent repo), requires 40-hex main/pilot pins, a clean checkout on branch 'main', HEAD parents exactly [main, pilot] in order, main ancestor-of pilot (check=True), and HEAD tree byte-identical to the reviewed pilot tree; it re-binds P001 scientific approval (verify_receipt on review.json), patient-adapter review, and archive review at integration time, and performs no merge, push, or dispatch.

VERIFIED (publication authority and recovery): workflow_boundary.publish is a compare-and-swap append: 40-hex source and expected-remote pins, HEAD==source, full check_pilot_publication audit of BASE..tip, ls-remote must return exactly the expected pin for the exact ref, expected_remote must be an ancestor of source (forbids rewind), and the push uses --force-with-lease against the expected old value so a concurrent remote move fails the lease. The audit refuses merges, contaminated-history reachability with an exact returncode-1 requirement (git errors fail closed), unlisted paths, non-regular file modes (blocks symlinks/submodules), >1.5MB or NUL-containing blobs, credential-like bytes, and executed notebook outputs; results-validate.yml's 'results' filename prefix is correctly exempted only via ALLOWED_FILES membership.

VERIFIED (privacy/approvals preserved): the 047 cleanup remains rehearsed-only (status REHEARSED_ONLY_REQUIRES_OPERATOR_APPROVAL, remote_operation_executed: false, exact leased command unexecuted); residual case-linked metadata in per_case_staging.csv, split_manifest.csv, and staging_audit.json is explicitly disclosed and reserved for a separate operator disposition rather than silently retained; r1's 11-vs-12 advertised-refs inconsistency is now resolved by labeling the 11-ref blob audit as historical (2026-09-05) while the current 2026-09-06 reconciliation records 12 advertised refs traversed; docs consistently state the merge is proposed, not performed, and pilot history/commit identities are preserved.

ADVISORY (check.yml content gap): workflow_policy validates check.yml's triggers, permissions, and checkout credential settings but not its 'uses:' action pins or 'run:' step contents, and its only secrets barrier is the substring 'secrets.', which the equivalent secrets['NAME'] index syntax evades; job 'permissions:' restrict the GITHUB_TOKEN, not access to the secrets context. Because check_pilot_publication allows content changes to .github/workflows/check.yml with no semantic validation, a mutated check.yml could pass workflow_policy while adding an unpinned third-party action or a secrets-referencing run step that executes on every push. Mitigated by the candidate-tree==reviewed-pilot-tree binding plus the contract's required human review of the final PR head. Recommend allowlisting check.yml's uses pins and broadening the secrets scan (e.g. refuse the bare token 'secrets').

ADVISORY (model-workflow step schema not fully closed): step-level keys other than name/run/uses and the checkout 'with' mapping (e.g. env, shell, continue-on-error, working-directory) are not constrained by workflow_policy. Impact appears nil today — the single run string is exact, actions are SHA-pinned, the terminal guard exits 1, and permissions are read-only — but env on the verify step is attacker-influenced YAML that the policy never inspects; the same secrets['NAME'] substring evasion applies. Tightening to an exact per-step key schema would fully close this.

MINOR: actioner.yml still advertises the stale propose_improvement input on a fully blocked job (carried over from r1; harmless). workflow_policy's guard execution uses timeout=5, whose TimeoutExpired propagates uncaught — fail-closed but an opaque failure mode.
